source_refs.note: Exercise 10.3, Question 1: book page 194 (PDF 199); answer key PDF 308 gives values for other data (both parts), boxed; checked with sympy and the solution book (PDF 933-936).

blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the values of \(\sin 2\alpha\), \(\cos 2\alpha\) and \(\tan 2\alpha\), when: \(\sin\alpha = \frac{84}{85}\)
blocks.explanation:
We know \(\sin\alpha\) and need the three ratios of the double angle \(2\alpha\).
The double-angle formulas need both \(\sin\alpha\) and \(\cos\alpha\).
Plan: find \(\cos\alpha\), then use \(\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\), \(\cos 2\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^2\alpha\), and divide for \(\tan 2\alpha\).
steps:
Given: \(\sin\alpha = \frac{84}{85}\). No quadrant is printed for part (i); the condition \(0 < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}\) printed with part (ii) is taken for both parts, so \(\alpha\) is acute.
To find: \(\sin 2\alpha\), \(\cos 2\alpha\), \(\tan 2\alpha\).
Method: \(\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1\) gives \(\cos\alpha\); then the double-angle identities of Section 10.4.

Find \(\cos\alpha\)
\[\cos^2\alpha = 1 - \left(\dfrac{84}{85}\right)^2\]
\[= \dfrac{7225 - 7056}{7225} = \dfrac{169}{7225}\]
\[\cos\alpha = \dfrac{13}{85}\]
Why: \(85^2 = 7225\), \(84^2 = 7056\), \(\sqrt{169} = 13\). We take the positive root because \(\alpha\) is in quadrant I.

Find \(\sin 2\alpha\)
\[\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\]
\[= 2 \cdot \dfrac{84}{85} \cdot \dfrac{13}{85}\]
\[= \dfrac{2184}{7225}\]
Why: Double-angle formula for sine; \(2 \times 84 \times 13 = 2184\).

Find \(\cos 2\alpha\)
\[\cos 2\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^2\alpha\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{2(7056)}{7225}\]
\[= \dfrac{7225 - 14112}{7225}\]
\[= -\dfrac{6887}{7225}\]
Why: This form uses only \(\sin\alpha\), which is given exactly.

Find \(\tan 2\alpha\)
\[\tan 2\alpha = \dfrac{\sin 2\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha}\]
\[= \dfrac{2184/7225}{-6887/7225}\]
\[= -\dfrac{2184}{6887}\]
Why: The common denominator 7225 cancels.

Check
\[2184^2 + 6887^2 = 52\,200\,625\]
\[7225^2 = 52\,200\,625 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(\sin^2 2\alpha + \cos^2 2\alpha\) must be 1. Also \(\sin\alpha > \cos\alpha\), so \(\alpha > 45^{\circ}\) and \(2\alpha > 90^{\circ}\): a negative \(\cos 2\alpha\) is expected.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\sin 2\alpha = \frac{120}{169}\), \(\cos 2\alpha = -\frac{119}{169}\), \(\tan 2\alpha = -\frac{120}{119}\). These belong to \(\sin\alpha = \frac{12}{13}\), not to the printed \(\sin\alpha = \frac{84}{85}\). The correct values are \(\frac{2184}{7225}\), \(-\frac{6887}{7225}\), \(-\frac{2184}{6887}\).

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the values of \(\sin 2\alpha\), \(\cos 2\alpha\) and \(\tan 2\alpha\), when: \(\cos\alpha = \frac{120}{169}\), where \(0 < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Same type as part (i), but this time \(\cos\alpha\) is given.
We must find \(\sin 2\alpha\), \(\cos 2\alpha\), \(\tan 2\alpha\).
Plan: find \(\sin\alpha\) (positive in quadrant I), then use the double-angle formulas.
steps:
Given: \(\cos\alpha = \frac{120}{169}\), \(0 < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}\).
To find: \(\sin 2\alpha\), \(\cos 2\alpha\), \(\tan 2\alpha\).
Method: \(\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1\) gives \(\sin\alpha\); then \(\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\) and \(\cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^2\alpha - 1\).

Find \(\cos 2\alpha\)
\[\cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^2\alpha - 1\]
\[= \dfrac{2(14400)}{28561} - 1\]
\[= \dfrac{28800 - 28561}{28561} = \dfrac{239}{28561}\]
Why: This form uses only the given \(\cos\alpha\).

Find \(\tan 2\alpha\)
\[\tan 2\alpha = \dfrac{28560}{239}\]
Why: Divide \(\sin 2\alpha\) by \(\cos 2\alpha\); the denominator 28561 cancels.

Check
\[28561^2 - 28560^2 = 28561 + 28560\]
\[= 57121 = 239^2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(\sin^2 2\alpha + \cos^2 2\alpha = 1\) means \(28560^2 + 239^2 = 28561^2\); the difference of squares shows it. Also \(\cos\alpha > \sin\alpha\), so \(\alpha < 45^{\circ}\) and all three values are positive.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\sin 2\alpha = \frac{24}{25}\), \(\cos 2\alpha = -\frac{7}{25}\), \(\tan 2\alpha = -\frac{24}{7}\). These belong to \(\cos\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\), not to the printed \(\cos\alpha = \frac{120}{169}\). The correct values are \(\frac{28560}{28561}\), \(\frac{239}{28561}\), \(\frac{28560}{239}\).
